Hinc et sanctus Job dixit : Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit. Per Zachariam quoque Dominus loquitur : Ducam eos per ignem, et uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum. Unde et Judith ait : Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Hinc igitur discamus patientiam, et in adversis sicut in omnibus divitiis gloriemur.
paras.en: [[3:6|As gold in the furnace, he hath proved them|Tanquam aurum in fornace probavit illos]]: that is, as gold is tested in the fire of the furnace, whether it be true and good gold, and is there purged of the dross mixed with it and made brighter; so God proved his elect in the fire of adversity, and showed them proved, made them purer, and brought them to the brightness of eternal salvation: and though the bodies of some were burnt with fire or devoured by beasts, yet their souls were endowed with greater grace and glory. Hence holy Job too said: The Lord [[Job 23:10|has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire|Probavit me Dominus quasi aurum quod per ignem transit]]. Through Zacharias also the Lord says: [[Zach 13:9|I will bring|Ducam eos]] them [[Zach 13:9|through the fire|per ignem]], [[Zach 13:9|and will refine them as silver is refined: and I will try them as gold is tried|et uram eos sicut uritur argentum, et probabo eos sicut probatur aurum]]. Hence Judith too says: [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui Deo placuerunt, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. Let us then learn patience from this, and glory in adversity as in all riches.

paras.t: Et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos : id est, sicut sacrificium legis quod holocaustum vocatum est, quia ad divinæ majestatis honorem totaliter incendebatur ac cremabatur, in signum quod homo se totum debet Deo ac cultui ejus : sicut, inquam, sacrificium illud fuit Deo acceptum ex offerentium fide, caritate et devotione; sic martyres sancti et viri perfecti, Deo valde accepti fuerunt per hoc quod ex fidei sinceritate, caritatis fervore, et devotionis fragrantia, se ipsos Deo totaliter obtulerunt per martyrii passionem aut cultum perfectum. Ideo scriptum est : Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors Sanctorum ejus.
paras.en: [[3:6|and as a victim of a holocaust, he hath received them|Et quasi holocausti hostiam accepit illos]]: that is, as the sacrifice of the law that was called a holocaust, because it was wholly burnt and consumed to the honour of the divine majesty, in sign that man owes his whole self to God and to his worship; as that sacrifice, I say, was acceptable to God by reason of the faith, charity and devotion of those who offered it; so the holy martyrs and perfect men were very acceptable to God, in that out of sincerity of faith, fervour of charity and fragrance of devotion they offered themselves wholly to God, through the suffering of martyrdom or through perfect worship. Therefore it is written: [[Ps 115:6|Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints|Pretiosa in conspectu Domini mors Sanctorum ejus]] [the margin gives Ps. cxv, 15, numbering this psalm on from Ps 114; here it is Ps 115:6].

paras.t: Et in tempore erit respectus illorum : id est, quamvis Deus ad tempus permittat electos suos ita affligi, tamen tempore opportuno, et ab ipso præordinato, ipsos clementer adspiciet, et ab omni pœna ereptos, gloriose ac copiose coronabit ac præmiabit. Ideo in Apocalypsi ait : Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ; atque in Psalmo : Cum ipso sum in tribulatione; eripiam eum et glorificabo eum. Denique, In tempore erit respectus illorum, id est, qui nunc in pœnis et persecutionibus videntur viles, et quasi a Deo relicti, in die judicii conspicientur ab omnibus gloriosi. Ideo subditur :
paras.en: [[3:6|And in time there shall be respect had to them|Et in tempore erit respectus illorum]]: that is, although God for a time allows his elect to be so afflicted, yet at the fitting time, foreordained by him, he will look upon them with mercy and, having snatched them from all pain, will crown and reward them gloriously and abundantly. Therefore he says in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 2:10|Be thou faithful unto death: and I will give thee the crown of life|Esto fidelis usque ad mortem, et dabo tibi coronam vitæ]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him, and I will glorify him|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione; eripiam eum et glorificabo eum]]. Lastly, [[3:6|in time there shall be respect had to them|In tempore erit respectus illorum]]: that is, those who now in pains and persecutions seem vile, and as it were forsaken by God, will in the day of judgement be seen by all in glory. Therefore it is added:

paras.t: Fulgebunt justi in corporibus glorificatis, in die extremi judicii et deinceps in cœlestis gloria paradisi, per dotem claritatis. Incomparabiliter vero clarius fulgebunt in corde, per lumen gloriæ et beatificam visionem immediate conjuncti lumini increato : quod erit eis objectum, et quasi forma ac medium cognoscendi Deum, qui non per speciem creatam, sed increatam, videtur clare et immediate facie ad faciem. Hinc asserit etiam Dominus : Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum. Et rursus Deus apud Malachiam testatur : Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ. Et tanquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent : id est, per dotem agilitatis erunt celerrime mobiles, sicut scintillæ velocissime agitantur in arundineto, videlicet in loco quo cannæ nascuntur. Idcirco ait Deus per Malachiam : Salietis quasi vituli de armento. Et sicut ignis cito consumit arundinetum, sic Sancti in die judicii velocissime dijudicabunt iniquos. Unde subjungitur :
paras.en: [[3:7|The just shall shine|Fulgebunt justi]] in their glorified bodies, in the day of the last judgement and thenceforth in the glory of the heavenly paradise, by the endowment of brightness [one of the four endowments of the glorified body: brightness, agility, subtlety and impassibility]. But they shall shine incomparably more brightly in heart, by the light of glory and the beatific vision, joined without any medium to the uncreated light: which will be their object, and as it were the form and the medium of knowing God, who is seen not through a created species [that is, a likeness through which a thing is known] but through the uncreated one, clearly and without medium, [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]]. Hence the Lord too declares: [[Matt 13:43|Then shall the just shine as the sun, in the kingdom of their Father|Fulgebunt justi sicut sol in regno Patris eorum]]. And again God testifies in Malachias: [[Mal 4:2|unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise|Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ]]. [[3:7|And shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds|Et tanquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent]]: that is, by the endowment of agility they shall move most swiftly, as sparks dart most swiftly about in a reed-bed, that is, in a place where canes grow. Therefore God says through Malachias: You [[Mal 4:2|shall leap like calves of the herd|Salietis quasi vituli de armento]]. And as fire quickly consumes a reed-bed, so the Saints in the day of judgement will most swiftly judge the wicked. Hence it is added:

paras.t: Judicabunt nationes : quoniam assessoria dignitate, et approbatione sententiæ judicabunt cum Domino Salvatore, qui cunctis Sanctis promisit : Vos qui secuti estis me, sedebitis super sedes, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel. Judicabunt ergo nationes, id est omnes reprobos et iniquos. Propter quod ait Apostolus : An nescitis quia Sancti de hoc mundo judicabunt? Et Psalmista : Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum, ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus. Et dominabuntur populis. Jam interim habent dominium super existentes in sæculo isto; et in die judicii apparebunt judices ac domini persecutorum suorum ac omnium iniquorum. Hinc in Propheta legitur : Egrediemini, et calcabitis impios. In Apocalypsi quoque asserit Christus : Qui vicerit, et qui custodierit usque in finem opera mea, dabo illi potestatem super gentes; et reget eas in virga ferrea, et tanquam vas figuli confringentur. Et regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum, et ipsi cum Domino suo, Dominusque cum eis, quemadmodum Judex in Apocalypsi testatur : Qui vicerit, dabo ei sedere mecum in throno meo, sicut et ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus. Hinc fertur in Daniele : Regnum et potestas dabitur populo Sanctorum Altissimi.
paras.en: [[3:8|They shall judge nations|Judicabunt nationes]]: for by the dignity of assessors [that is, of those who sit beside the judge and share in his judgement], and by approving the sentence, they shall judge with the Lord the Saviour, who promised to all the Saints: [[Matt 19:28|you who have followed me|Vos qui secuti estis me]], [[Matt 19:28|shall sit on twelve seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel|sedebitis super sedes, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel]]. [[3:8|They shall judge nations|Judicabunt ergo nationes]], then, that is, all the reprobate and wicked. For this reason the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 6:2|Know you not that the saints shall judge this world?|An nescitis quia Sancti de hoc mundo judicabunt?]] And the Psalmist: [[Ps 149:6|two-edged swords in their hands|Gladii ancipites in manibus eorum]], [[Ps 149:7|To execute vengeance upon the nations|ad faciendam vindictam in nationibus]]. [[3:8|And rule over people|Et dominabuntur populis]]. Even now, in the meantime, they have dominion over those who live in this world; and in the day of judgement they will appear as judges and lords of their persecutors and of all the wicked. Hence we read in the Prophet: [[Mal 4:2|you shall go forth|Egrediemini]], [[Mal 4:3|and you shall tread down the wicked|et calcabitis impios]]. In the Apocalypse too Christ declares: [[Apoc 2:26|he that shall overcome and keep my works unto the end, I will give him power over the nations|Qui vicerit, et qui custodierit usque in finem opera mea, dabo illi potestatem super gentes]]; [[Apoc 2:27|And he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and as the vessel of a potter they shall be broken|et reget eas in virga ferrea, et tanquam vas figuli confringentur]]. [[3:8|And their Lord shall reign for ever|Et regnabit Dominus illorum in perpetuum]], and they with their Lord, and the Lord with them, as the Judge testifies in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:21|To him that shall overcome, I will give to sit with me in my throne: as I also have overcome and am set down with my Father in his throne|Qui vicerit, dabo ei sedere mecum in throno meo, sicut et ego vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus]]. Hence it is said in Daniel: [[Dan 7:27|The kingdom, and power|Regnum et potestas]] [[Dan 7:27|may be given to the people of the saints of the most High|dabitur populo Sanctorum Altissimi]].

paras.t: Qui confidunt in illo, intelligent veritatem : id est, qui cum humili fiducia invocant Deum constanter pro illuminatione interna, intelligent veritatem de necessariis ad salutem, quia Dominus illuminabit eos per se, aut per suos ministros. Quis enim invocavit illum, et despexit eum? Ideo monet Apostolus : Adeamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus. Nempe qui confidunt in Domino, non præsumunt de ingenio suo, ideo illuminari merentur. Propterea hortatur Propheta : Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini. Et fideles in dilectione, id est, qui Deum constanter et efficaciter diligunt, acquiescent illi, id est, obedient, adhærebunt, et suum intellectum humiliter subdent auctoritati fidei ac Scripturis, redigentes intellectum suum in captivitatem, in obsequium Christi. Hinc ait Salvator : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit; et alibi, Si præcepta mea servaveritis, manebitis in dilectione mea. Etenim signum fidelis et veræ dilectionis, est exhibitio operis. Dilectio enim conformat voluntatem diligentis voluntati dilecti, et quasi ligat eas ad invicem, quia dilectio dicitur quasi duorum ligatio. Quoniam donum et pax est electis ejus : id est, electi Dei habent a Deo dona gratiæ, pacemque pectoris in præsenti, ac dona gloriæ ac pacem æternitatis in futuro. Denique electis seu prædestinatis Deus largitur in via omnia necessaria pro beatitudine obtinenda, quemadmodum ab æterno decrevit et præordinavit.
paras.en: [[3:9|They that trust in him shall understand the truth|Qui confidunt in illo, intelligent veritatem]]: that is, those who with humble confidence call upon God constantly for inward enlightenment shall understand the truth about the things necessary for salvation, because the Lord will enlighten them by himself or by his ministers. For [[Ecclus 2:12|who hath called upon him, and he despised him?|Quis enim invocavit illum, et despexit eum?]] Therefore the Apostle warns: [[Heb 4:16|Let us go|Adeamus]] [[Heb 4:16|with confidence to the throne of grace|cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ]]. For those who trust in the Lord do not presume on their own wit, and so they deserve to be enlightened. For this reason the Prophet exhorts: [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini]]. [[3:9|And they that are faithful in love|Et fideles in dilectione]], that is, who love God constantly and effectually, [[3:9|shall rest in him|acquiescent illi]] [acquiescent means both 'rest in' and 'yield assent to'], that is, they shall obey him, cleave to him, and humbly subject their understanding to the authority of the faith and to the Scriptures, [[2 Cor 10:5|bringing into captivity|redigentes intellectum suum in captivitatem]] their understanding [[2 Cor 10:5|unto the obedience of Christ|in obsequium Christi]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit]]; and elsewhere, [[John 15:10|If you keep my commandments, you shall abide in my love|Si præcepta mea servaveritis, manebitis in dilectione mea]]. For the sign of faithful and true love is the showing of it in deed. For love conforms the will of the lover to the will of the beloved, and as it were binds them to each other, since love is called as it were a binding of two [dilectio, as though duorum ligatio: a play on the words]. [[3:9|For grace and peace are to his elect|Quoniam donum et pax est electis ejus]]: that is, the elect of God have from God the gifts of grace and peace of heart in the present, and the gifts of glory and the peace of eternity in the future. Lastly, to the elect or predestined God grants on the way all things necessary for obtaining beatitude, as he decreed and foreordained from eternity.

paras.t: Impii autem secundum quæ cogitaverunt, correptionem habebunt, id est, debitas luent pœnas, et in judicio corripientur secundum cogitationum suarum demerita. Illis etenim Judex dicturus est : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Qui neglexerunt justum, id est, Deum essentialiter justum, et justa ejus præcepta omiserunt. Hinc apud Sophoniam præcipitur : Quærite justum, quærite mansuetum, si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini. Et a Domino recesserunt per mentis aversionem et inobedientiam, non per localem distantiam : juxta illud, Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo.
paras.en: [[3:10|But the wicked shall be punished according to their own devices|Impii autem secundum quæ cogitaverunt, correptionem habebunt]], that is, they shall pay the penalties due, and in the judgement shall be chastised according to the demerits of their thoughts. For the Judge will say to them: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. [[3:10|Who have neglected the just|Qui neglexerunt justum]], that is, God, who is just in his essence, and have left his just precepts undone. Hence in Sophonias it is commanded: [[Soph 2:3|seek the just, seek the meek: if by any means you may be hid in the day of the Lord's indignation|Quærite justum, quærite mansuetum, si quo modo abscondamini in die furoris Domini]]. [[3:10|And have revolted from the Lord|Et a Domino recesserunt]] by the turning away of the mind and by disobedience, not by distance of place: according to that, [[Osee 4:10|they have forsaken the Lord in not observing the law|Dereliquerunt Dominum in non custodiendo]].

paras.t: Sapientiam enim, quæ est sapida divinorum notitia, et disciplinam, id est moralia documenta, seu correptionem caritativam, justamve castigationem, qui abjicit a se, infelix est jam miseriis culpæ, et demeritis pœnæ æternæ. Hoc autem faciunt, qui recedunt a Domino. Hinc et in Proverbiis scriptum est : Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis. Apostolus quoque : Si extra disciplinam, inquit, estis, ergo adulteri, et non filii estis. Et vacua est spes illorum : quia inaniter sperant obtinere salutem, et in rebus caducis damnabiliter figunt spem suam, et frustrabuntur fine optato seu bono sperato; et labores sine fructu, id est, profectu et merito vitæ æternæ carent labores ipsorum : imo vitiosi sunt, et damnationem merentur, quum sit perversa eorum intentio; et inhabitabilia opera ipsorum : id est, ipsi per opera sua perversa, nec in militanti Ecclesia habitant, tanquam viva membra ad mysticum corpus Christi spectantia, nec cœlestem mansionem acquirent per ea. Idcirco de non confidente in Domino, et recedente ab eo, loquitur Jeremias : Erit tanquam myricæ in deserto, et habitabit in terra salsuginis. Tales namque ad ecclesiam malignantium, et ad Babylonicam pertinent civitatem.
paras.en: [[3:11|For he that rejecteth wisdom|Sapientiam enim]], which is the savoury knowledge of divine things [sapida, 'savoury', a play on sapientia], [[3:11|and discipline|et disciplinam]], that is, moral teachings, or charitable correction, or just chastisement, [[3:11|is unhappy|qui abjicit a se, infelix est]], already by the miseries of guilt, and by the demerits of eternal punishment. And this is what they do who revolt from the Lord. Hence it is written in Proverbs too: [[Prov 15:32|He that rejecteth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that yieldeth to reproof, possesseth understanding|Qui abjicit disciplinam, despicit animam suam; qui autem acquiescit increpationibus, possessor est cordis]]. The Apostle too: [[Heb 12:8|if you be without chastisement|Si extra disciplinam]], he says, [[Heb 12:8|then are you bastards and not sons|estis, ergo adulteri, et non filii estis]] [disciplinam, the same word as discipline in the verse]. [[3:11|And their hope is vain|Et vacua est spes illorum]]: because they hope in vain to obtain salvation, and damnably fix their hope on things that perish, and they shall be cheated of the end they long for, or of the good they hope for; [[3:11|and their labours without fruit|et labores sine fructu]], that is, their labours lack the profit and merit of eternal life: nay, they are vicious and deserve damnation, since their intention is perverse; [[3:11|and their works unprofitable|et inhabitabilia opera ipsorum]] [Denis reads inhabitabilia, 'not to be dwelt in', where the Vulgate has inutilia, 'unprofitable'], that is, through their perverse works they neither dwell in the Church militant, as living members belonging to the mystical body of Christ, nor will they gain a heavenly mansion by them. Therefore Jeremias says of him who does not trust in the Lord and revolts from him: [[Jer 17:6|he shall be like tamaric in the desert|Erit tanquam myricæ in deserto]], and [[Jer 17:6|he shall dwell|habitabit]] [[Jer 17:6|in a salt land|in terra salsuginis]]. For such belong to the church of the malignant and to the city of Babylon.

paras.t: Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt, conformando se vitiis maritorum suorum : quod tamen non semper sic est, sed frequenter. Et juxta hunc sensum subjungitur : et nequissimi filii eorum : quia a parentibus non informantur, nec educantur in salubri scientia, et moribus atque virtutibus, sed magis in vitiis.
paras.en: [[3:12|Their wives are foolish|Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt]], by conforming themselves to the vices of their husbands: which however is not always so, but often. And in keeping with this sense it is added: [[3:12|and their children wicked|et nequissimi filii eorum]]: because they are not formed by their parents, nor brought up in wholesome knowledge, in good conduct and virtues, but rather in vices.

paras.t: Maledicta creatura eorum, id est posteritas, sive domestici vel cognati pertinentes ad eos, et eis consimiles : qui cum perversis pervertuntur, et majorum suorum sectantur prava vestigia. Quoniam felix sterilis et incoinquinata : id est, quæ talem non habet sobolem, felix est, et felicior quam si fecunda esset hujusmodi prole : quemadmodum et in Ecclesiastico scriptum est, Melius est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere post se filios nequam. Nam et turpe est parentibus, tam indisciplinatam et vitiosam habere prolem, præsertim dum ex parentum negligentia oritur infrenata malitia sobolis. Et inde multum augebitur parentum damnatio, in quos utique filiorum redundant peccata. Felix, inquam, sterilis, dummodo aliunde non exsistat culpabilis. Propterea additum est, Et incoinquinata, id est mortali vitio non fœdata.
paras.en: [[3:13|Their offspring is cursed|Maledicta creatura eorum]], that is, their posterity, or the members of their household or kinsfolk who belong to them and are like them: who with the perverse are perverted[[Ps 17:27||]], and follow the crooked footsteps of their elders. [[3:13|For happy is the barren|Quoniam felix sterilis]] [[3:13|and the undefiled|et incoinquinata]]: that is, she who has no such offspring is happy, and happier than if she were fruitful with offspring of this kind: as it is written in Ecclesiasticus too, [[Ecclus 16:4|it is better to die without children, than to leave ungodly children|Melius est mori sine filiis, quam relinquere post se filios nequam]]. For it is also a shame to parents to have offspring so undisciplined and vicious, especially when the unbridled malice of the offspring springs from the parents' negligence. And thereby the damnation of the parents will be much increased, since the sins of the children redound upon them. [[3:13|Happy is the barren|Felix, inquam, sterilis]], I say, provided she be not guilty on some other account. Therefore it is added, [[3:13|and the undefiled|Et incoinquinata]], that is, not defiled by mortal vice.

paras.t: Quæ nescivit torum in delicto, id est, adulterium non commisit, vel carnalem conjugalemque copulam non est experta, ita quod virgo permansit. Vel, Nescivit torum in delicto, id est, quamvis exstitit maritata, non tamen abusa est conjugio in peccatum, voluptatem quærendo, aut alio modo, sed solum reddendo debitum, aut desiderio prolis ad Dei obsequium educandæ, seu causa vitandi incontinentiam in conjugali : sicque implevit illud Apostoli, Honorabile connubium, et torus immaculatus.
paras.en: [[3:13|That hath not known bed in sin|Quæ nescivit torum in delicto]], that is, has not committed adultery, or has not known carnal and conjugal union, so that she remained a virgin. Or, [[3:13|hath not known bed in sin|Nescivit torum in delicto]], that is, though she was married, yet she did not abuse marriage to sin, by seeking pleasure or in some other way, but used it only in rendering the debt [that is, the marriage due owed to the spouse], or from desire of offspring to be brought up for the service of God, or to avoid incontinence in her spouse: and so she fulfilled that saying of the Apostle, [[Heb 13:4|Marriage honourable|Honorabile connubium]], [[Heb 13:4|and the bed undefiled|et torus immaculatus]].

paras.t: Habebit fructum, id est spiritualem profectum, atque internæ munditiæ incrementum in via, æternæ quoque beatitudinis remunerationem in patria, in respectione animarum sanctarum, id est ex divinæ pietatis respectu et infusione : quibus Deus adspicit, intuendoque implet animas virtuosas. De quo respectu dixit beatissima Virgo : Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ; et Dominus : Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum et contritum? Hinc et Christus in Evangelio castitati virginali promittit fructum centesimum, castitati viduali sexagesimum, conjugali tricesimum : Semen, inquiens, cecidit in terram bonam, et ortum, fecit fructum, aliud centesimum, aliud sexagesimum, aliud tricesimum.
paras.en: [[3:13|She shall have fruit|Habebit fructum]], that is, spiritual progress and increase of inward cleanness on the way, and also the reward of eternal beatitude in the fatherland, [[3:13|in the visitation of holy souls|in respectione animarum sanctarum]] [respectio, literally a 'looking upon' or 'regard'], that is, from the regard and infusion of the divine mercy, by which God looks upon virtuous souls and, in beholding them, fills them. Of this regard the most blessed Virgin said: [[Luke 1:48|Because he hath regarded the humility of his handmaid|Quia respexit humilitatem ancillæ suæ]]; and the Lord: [[Is 66:2|To whom shall I have respect, but to him that is poor and little|Ad quem respiciam, nisi ad pauperculum]] and contrite? Hence Christ too in the Gospel promises to virginal chastity the hundredfold fruit, to the chastity of widows the sixtyfold, to married chastity the thirtyfold: The seed, he says, [[Matt 13:8|fell upon good ground|cecidit in terram bonam]], [[Luke 8:8|and, being sprung up, yielded fruit|et ortum, fecit fructum]], [[Matt 13:8|some an hundred fold, some sixty fold, and some thirty fold|aliud centesimum, aliud sexagesimum, aliud tricesimum]].

paras.t: Et spado, qui non operatus est per manus suas, id est vires operativas, iniquitatem, peccando verbis aut factis, nec cogitavit adversum Deum nequissima, id est, per cogitationes pravas Deum non offendit, dolendo de impotentia sua, et voluptates optando. Dicitur equidem spado, impotens coeundi, seu eunuchus castratus : et tales quandoque corrupti ac libidinosi sunt mente, sicut in Ecclesiastico legitur : Spado complectens virginem, et suspirans. Talis, inquam, spado est felix, quamvis corporaliter sterilis; estque felicior vitiosis parentibus sobolis pravæ. Dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum, id est præclarum munus puritatis internæ ac interioris profectus, ad quod per fidem pertingitur, atque post hujus incolatum exsilii, donum gloriæ æternalis; et sors in templo Dei acceptissima, id est gratissima portio supernorum charismatum in militanti ac triumphanti Ecclesia. Nec ab ingressu excludetur materialis ecclesiæ, sicut in lege, juxta illud in Deuteronomio : Non intrabit eunuchus in ecclesiam Dei.
paras.en: [[3:14|And the eunuch, that hath not wrought|Et spado, qui non operatus est]] [[3:14|with his hands|per manus suas]], that is, with his working powers, [[3:14|iniquity|iniquitatem]], by sinning in words or deeds, [[3:14|nor thought wicked things against God|nec cogitavit adversum Deum nequissima]], that is, has not offended God by wicked thoughts, grieving over his impotence and longing for pleasures. Now a spado [the word rendered eunuch] is one who is incapable of intercourse, or a castrated eunuch: and such men are sometimes corrupt and lustful in mind, as we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 30:21|an eunuch embracing a virgin, and sighing|Spado complectens virginem, et suspirans]]. Such a eunuch, I say, is happy, though bodily barren; and he is happier than the vicious parents of wicked offspring. [[3:14|For the precious gift of faith shall be given to him|Dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum]] [electum, literally 'choice'], that is, the excellent gift of inward purity and of interior progress, which is reached through faith, and, after the sojourn of this exile, the gift of eternal glory; [[3:14|and a most acceptable lot in the temple of God|et sors in templo Dei acceptissima]], that is, a most welcome portion of the heavenly gifts of grace in the Church militant and triumphant. Nor shall he be shut out from entering the material church, as he was under the law, according to that in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:1|An eunuch|Non intrabit eunuchus]] [[Deut 23:1|shall not enter into the church of the Lord|in ecclesiam Dei]].

paras.t: Bonorum enim laborum, qui ex caritate procedunt, assumuntur aut tolerantur, gloriosus est fructus, id est retributio copiosa ac felix. Propter quod monet et Apostolus : Stabiles estote, abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino. Et alibi scriptum est : Non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro. Et Paulus rursus loquitur : Unusquisque recipiet secundum suum laborem. Et quæ non concidat radix sapientiæ, id est, habitus seu donum sapientiæ stabilis, quæ manet in patria, spadoni tali præstabitur. Talis etenim, quum careat vitiis carnis, nec impugnetur ab eis, ad contemplationem est aptus : cujus radix et origo, est sapientiæ donum; cujus actus, est contemplatio ipsa. Et hæc radix sapientiæ dicitur non concidere, quemadmodum caritas non excidere perhibetur.
paras.en: [[3:15|For the fruit of good labours|Bonorum enim laborum]], those which proceed from charity and are taken up or endured, [[3:15|is glorious|gloriosus est fructus]], that is, the reward is abundant and happy. For which reason the Apostle too warns: [[1 Cor 15:58|be ye steadfast|Stabiles estote]], [[1 Cor 15:58|always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord|abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino]]. And elsewhere it is written: [[2 Par 15:7|let not your hands be weakened: for there shall be a reward for your work|Non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro]]. And Paul again says: [[1 Cor 3:8|every man shall receive|Unusquisque recipiet]] [[1 Cor 3:8|according to his own labour|secundum suum laborem]]. [[3:15|And the root of wisdom never faileth|Et quæ non concidat radix sapientiæ]], that is, the abiding habit or gift of wisdom, which remains in the fatherland, shall be bestowed on such a eunuch. For such a one, since he is free of the vices of the flesh and is not assailed by them, is fitted for contemplation: whose root and origin is the gift of wisdom, and whose act is contemplation itself. And this root of wisdom is said not to fail, as charity is said not to fall away[[1 Cor 13:8||]].

paras.t: Filii autem adulterorum, qui parentum vitia imitantur, sive corporaliter, sive spiritualiter adulteri sint (et præsertim in lege idololatria appellatur adulterium seu fornicatio spiritualis), in consummatione erunt, id est, extremæ damnationi, quæ est vitiorum consummatio ac merces finalis, adjudicabuntur. Juxta quem modum legitur ad Hebræos : Cujus consummatio in combustione erit. Et ab iniquo toro semen exterminabitur, id est, soboles nata a toro seu conjugibus vitiosis, de electorum numero auferetur, si parentum vitia imitetur. Vel sensus est, quod conjugati iniqui, propter sua demerita privabuntur prolis fecunditate. Quemadmodum enim in lege promittebatur justis fecunditas, juxta illud Deuteronomii, Benedictus fructus uteri tui; et in Psalmo, Uxor tua sicut vitis abundans in lateribus domus tuæ : sic fecunditatis privatio quandoque pro culpa irrogabatur.
paras.en: [[3:16|But the children of adulterers|Filii autem adulterorum]], who imitate the vices of their parents, whether these be adulterers bodily or spiritually (and in the law especially idolatry is called adultery or spiritual fornication[[Ex 34:15||]][[Ex 34:16||]][[Lev 17:7||]][[Lev 20:5||]]), [[3:16|shall not come to perfection|in consummatione erunt]] [Denis's text reads in consummatione erunt, 'shall be in consummation', where the Vulgate has in inconsummatione, 'shall be unfinished'; he takes it of their last end], that is, they shall be adjudged to final damnation, which is the consummation and last wages of vices. In the same way we read in the Epistle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 6:8|whose end is to be burnt|Cujus consummatio in combustione erit]] [consummatio, 'end', the same word]. [[3:16|And the seed of the unlawful bed shall be rooted out|Et ab iniquo toro semen exterminabitur]], that is, the offspring born of a vicious bed, that is, of vicious spouses, shall be taken away from the number of the elect, if it imitate the vices of its parents. Or the sense is that wicked married people shall for their demerits be deprived of fruitfulness in offspring. For as in the law fruitfulness was promised to the just, according to that of Deuteronomy, [[Deut 28:4|Blessed shall be the fruit of thy womb|Benedictus fructus uteri tui]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 127:3|Thy wife as a fruitful vine, on the sides of thy house|Uxor tua sicut vitis abundans in lateribus domus tuæ]]: so the loss of fruitfulness was sometimes inflicted for sin.

paras.t: Et si quidem longæ vitæ erunt, id est, dato quod tales iniqui diu vivant in carne, in nihilum computabuntur, id est, nullius virtuositatis aut ponderis erunt : imo, quo diutius vixerint, eo viliores deterioresque apparebunt; et sine honore erit novissima senectus illorum. Honor quippe est exhibitio reverentiæ in signum testimoniumque virtutis : ideo, sicut carebunt virtute, sic et honore in senio. Quamvis enim senectus ex se sit aliquo modo venerabilis, juxta illud Levitici, Honora personam senis; tamen propter vitia puerilitatis, seu perversitatis ei adjuncta, fit aspernabilis. Propter quod Isaias ait : Puer centum annorum morietur, et peccator centum annorum maledictus erit.
paras.en: [[3:17|And if they live long|Et si quidem longæ vitæ erunt]], that is, granted that such wicked men live long in the flesh, [[3:17|they shall be nothing regarded|in nihilum computabuntur]], that is, they will be of no virtue or weight: nay, the longer they have lived, the viler and worse they will appear; [[3:17|and their last old age shall be without honour|et sine honore erit novissima senectus illorum]]. For honour is the showing of reverence in sign and testimony of virtue: therefore, as they will lack virtue, so they will lack honour in old age. For although old age is of itself in some way venerable, according to that of Leviticus, [[Lev 19:32|honour the person of the aged man|Honora personam senis]], yet through the vices of childishness or of perversity joined to it, it becomes contemptible. For which reason Isaias says: [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed|Puer centum annorum morietur, et peccator centum annorum maledictus erit]].

paras.t: Et si celerius defuncti fuerint, non habebunt spem formatam felicitatis futuræ, nec ipsam spei rem consequentur, nec in die agnitionis allocutionem : id est, in die judicii universalis seu particularis, quando cuncta eorum peccata pandentur, non poterunt pro se reddere rationem, nec Judici respondere; nec approbationis sententiam audient ab eodem, qua dicet : Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi.
paras.en: [[3:18|And if they die quickly|Et si celerius defuncti fuerint]], [[3:18|they shall have no hope|non habebunt spem]], no formed hope [that is, hope given life by charity] of future happiness, nor shall they obtain the thing hoped for itself, [[3:18|nor speech of comfort in the day of trial|nec in die agnitionis allocutionem]] [agnitionis, literally 'of recognition'; allocutio, 'a speaking to'], that is, in the day of judgement, universal or particular, when all their sins shall be laid bare, they will not be able to render an account for themselves, nor to answer the Judge; nor will they hear from him the sentence of approval, by which he will say: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father, possess you the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world|Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi]].

paras.t: Nationes enim iniquæ, diræ sunt consummationis, id est, crudelem habebunt finem, et damnationem asperrimam. Quibus dicetur : Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum.
paras.en: [[3:19|For dreadful are the ends of a wicked race|Nationes enim iniquæ, diræ sunt consummationis]] [Denis's text reads: for wicked nations are of a dreadful end], that is, they shall have a cruel end and a most bitter damnation. To them it shall be said: [[Matt 25:41|Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire|Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum]].

paras.t: Præterea, ab illo loco, Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt, possunt hæc spiritualiter interpretari : ita quod mulieres iniquorum, id est sensualitates, insensatæ sunt, quia rationi rebelles; nequissimi quoque filii, id est actus eorum : quia ex habitu prodeunt vitioso. Maledicta creatura eorum, id est conversatio ab ipsis egrediens. Creare enim, frequenter accipitur pro facere seu formare. Quoniam felix sterilis et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit torum in delicto. Hoc de virginibus specialiter accipi potest, et de qualibet anima casta quæ nec in hæresim, nec in idololatriam, neque in mortalis peccati corruptionem est lapsa : quæ in futuro sequetur Agnum quocumque perrexerit. Et spado qui non operatus est iniquitatem. Quocirca loquitur Glossa : Potest in sterili et spadone ordo virginum designari : de quo fertur in Isaia : Non dicat eunuchus, Ecce ego lignum aridum. Et talem fuisse eunuchum Joannem apostolum, ecclesiasticæ tradunt historiæ : qui ausus est dicere quod sæcula nescierunt, In principio erat Verbum. Deficit ergo calumniatio Judæorum, quæ semiviris aperit regnum cœlorum, quum pudicitia sit in voluntate animi, non in corporis debilitate. Dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum. Unde in Evangelio Christus : Sunt, inquit, eunuchi qui se ipsos castraverunt propter regnum cœlorum; non omnes capiunt verbum hoc, sed quibus datum est. Hinc legitur et in Isaia : Hæc dicit Dominus eunuchis : Qui custodierint sabbata mea, et elegerint quæ volui, dabo eis in domo mea locum, et nomen melius a filiis et filiabus. Filii autem adulterorum spirituali adulterio, puta discipuli hæresiarcharum et omnium vitiosorum imitatores, in consummatione damnationis erunt : sicut expositum est. Postremo, omnis anima cœlesti Sponso per fidem et gratiam in Baptismate consecrata, mortaliter peccans, adultera est diaboli : quæ cum imitantibus se peribit.
paras.en: Moreover, from the place [[3:12|Their wives are foolish|Mulieres eorum insensatæ sunt]] onwards, these words can be interpreted spiritually: so that the wives of the wicked, that is, their sensual powers, [[3:12|are foolish|insensatæ sunt]], because they rebel against reason; [[3:12|and their children wicked|nequissimi quoque filii]], that is, their acts, because these proceed from a vicious habit. [[3:13|Their offspring is cursed|Maledicta creatura eorum]] [creatura, literally 'what they create'], that is, the way of life that goes forth from them. For to create is often taken for to make or to form. [[3:13|for happy is the barren: and the undefiled, that hath not known bed in sin|Quoniam felix sterilis et incoinquinata, quæ nescivit torum in delicto]]. This can be taken especially of virgins, and of any chaste soul that has not fallen into heresy, nor into idolatry, nor into the corruption of mortal sin: which in the time to come shall [[Apoc 14:4|follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth|sequetur Agnum quocumque perrexerit]]. [[3:14|And the eunuch, that hath not wrought iniquity|Et spado qui non operatus est iniquitatem]]. On which the Gloss says: In the barren woman and the eunuch the order of virgins can be signified; of which it is said in Isaias: [[Is 56:3|let not the eunuch say: Behold I am a dry tree|Non dicat eunuchus, Ecce ego lignum aridum]]. And the histories of the Church relate that the apostle John was such a eunuch: he who dared to say what the ages had not known, [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. So the cavilling of the Jews fails before this teaching, which opens the kingdom of heaven to half-men [semiviris, that is, eunuchs], since chastity lies in the will of the mind, not in weakness of the body. [[3:14|For the precious gift of faith shall be given to him|Dabitur enim illi fidei donum electum]]. Hence Christ in the Gospel: [[Matt 19:12|There are|Sunt]], he says, [[Matt 19:12|eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven|eunuchi qui se ipsos castraverunt propter regnum cœlorum]]; [[Matt 19:11|All men take not this word, but they to whom it is given|non omnes capiunt verbum hoc, sed quibus datum est]]. Hence we read in Isaias too: [[Is 56:4|thus saith the Lord to the eunuchs, They that shall keep my sabbaths, and shall choose the things that please me|Hæc dicit Dominus eunuchis : Qui custodierint sabbata mea, et elegerint quæ volui]], [[Is 56:5|I will give to them in my house|dabo eis in domo mea]], [[Is 56:5|a place, and a name better than sons and daughters|locum, et nomen melius a filiis et filiabus]]. [[3:16|But the children of adulterers|Filii autem adulterorum]] by spiritual adultery, for instance the disciples of heresiarchs and the imitators of all vicious men, shall be in the consummation of damnation, as has been explained. Lastly, every soul consecrated to the heavenly Bridegroom through faith and grace in Baptism, if it sins mortally, is an adulteress of the devil: and with those who imitate her she shall perish.
